subject: Demo recap: model choices & risk assessment
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@finteq.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@finteq.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Demo recap: model choices & risk assessment

Hi Olivia / Daniel —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick written recap with the recommended model shortlist, the tradeoffs we discussed, and proposed next steps so your engineering team and procurement can align.

TL;DR recommended shortlist (for the PoC workload you shared):
- Redwood-Rouge-13B-q4
  - Latency (p50/p95): ~85ms / 180ms for 1k context on a T4-equivalent serving config
  - Cost estimate: $0.85 per 1k input+output tokens (hosted)
  - Quality: strong instruction-following on transactional prompts; lower hallucination than 7B but less knowledge depth than 70B options
  - Best when: you need balanced cost + consistent short-context accuracy

- Eleuthera-7B-int8
  - Latency (p50/p95): ~45ms / 120ms
  - Cost estimate: $0.32 per 1k tokens
  - Quality: very fast and cheap; may struggle with multi-step reasoning and long-context grounding
  - Best when: latency-sensitive paths (search augmentation, token-limited inference)

- OpenMosaic-70B-8bit
  - Latency (p50/p95): ~310ms / 650ms on A100-class nodes (Redwood Dedicated)
  - Cost estimate: $4.20 per 1k tokens
  - Quality: highest raw knowledge and fewest factual errors in our evals, but higher tail latency and cost
  - Best when: complex summarization, multi-turn contextual QA where accuracy is critical

Why these three: they span the production trade space you described (low-latency cheap, balanced, high-quality/heavier). For Finteq's use cases (real-time account summaries + downstream decisioning), our recommendation is to run parallel evals across these models with the following guardrails:
- Holdout prompt set (attached as prompt_set_v1.txt) that mirrors payment reconciliation and dispute resolution flows
- Long-context stress tests (see latency_benchmarks_50k_tokens.csv for representative numbers)
- Quality buckets: "Factuality", "Hallucination", "Actionability" — we'll score on those and highlight regressions vs baseline

Monitoring & rollback:
- We propose a 2-week canary with metric-based thresholds: if hallucination rate increase > 2% vs baseline OR customer-critical FTR (first-time-right) drops > 3pp, we automatically roll back to the previous model and open an incident.
- Redwood Console will expose token-level cost and per-route latency breakdowns so you can see real-time impact.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Finteq confirms target traffic slice and target SLOs for PoC (e.g., 100 req/s, p95 latency goal <= 400ms for critical paths) — please reply with numbers.
2) Redwood runs a 5-business-day evaluation across the three models using your prompt_set_v1 and the additional 50 holdout prompts we discussed.
3) We produce a short report (quality + cost + latency) and recommend a single model for rollout or a hybrid routing policy.
4) Procurement: if you want Dedicated capacity we can produce a draft order and SLA; otherwise hosted credits available for the PoC.

Attachments: prompt_set_v1.txt, latency_benchmarks_50k_tokens.csv, mutual_action_plan_Finteq_v1.pdf

If helpful, I can schedule a short 30-minute follow-up later this week to confirm the traffic targets and the eval cadence.

Thanks — looking forward.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Demo recap: model choices & risk assessment

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 
- Hallucination / factuality: do you have concrete numbers from your eval for similar finance doc/statement prompts? Even ballpark percentages would help our risk committee.
- Long context behavior: our workflows often include ~8–12k of context (statements + policy text). Can Eleuthera-7B-int8 really handle that without severe degradation?
- Fallback: if we run a hybrid policy, can requests automatically route to OpenMosaic-70B only when certain confidence thresholds are low?

We'll loop our engineering lead into the 30-minute follow-up once we confirm availability.

—Olivia
VP of Product, Finteq
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@finteq.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@finteq.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Demo recap: model choices & risk assessment

Great questions — answers below and a few configuration recommendations.

Hallucination/factuality:
- In our internal PoC evals on finance reconciliation prompts (similar structure to yours), measured hallucination (defined as any unsupported factual claim per our eval rubric) was: Redwood-Rouge-13B-q4 = 4.6%, Eleuthera-7B-int8 = 7.9%, OpenMosaic-70B-8bit = 2.1%. These are ballpark but based on a 2k-sample of holdout prompts; we'll run the same suite on your prompts for precise numbers.

Long-context handling:
- Eleuthera-7B-int8: performs best with active KV prefix caching for repeated document references, but single-request attention on 12k+ context will show degradation in multi-step chain-of-thought outputs. We recommend using it for short synthesis tasks and using Redwood-Rouge-13B-q4 or OpenMosaic for the long-context summarize/QA flows.

Routing/fallback:
- Yes — Redwood routing policies support confidence-based routing. Our suggestion: run Eleuthera for baseline queries; compute a lightweight model confidence score (we can instrument a simple heuristic we call "answer-certainty" during the canary). If certainty < 0.6 OR token length > 6k or the intent tag is "financial_dispute", route to OpenMosaic-70B. We can ship this as a config in the PoC.

Suggested trial configs to get meaningful comparison (we'll apply these in the 5-day run):
- Redwood-Rouge-13B-q4: temperature 0.0–0.2, max_tokens 512, enable prefix caching, batch size 8 for cost control
- Eleuthera-7B-int8: temperature 0.0, max_tokens 256, aggressive batching (continuous batching enabled) for p95 latency improvement
- OpenMosaic-70B-8bit: temperature 0.0–0.1, max_tokens 1024, Dedicated serving (A100) for stable tail latency

I've attached the prompt_set_v1.txt and latency_benchmarks_50k_tokens.csv for your review. Also shared the mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan_FInteq_v1.pdf) that lays out responsibilities and target dates — quick items from that doc:
- Confirm traffic slice and SLOs by Nov 10
- Start PoC evaluation (Redwood runs) Nov 15
- PoC report and model recommendation Nov 23

Next steps: can you confirm (by EOD Friday) the target traffic slice and whether your procurement team prefers a Hosted PoC (we'll bill usage) or a short-term Dedicated trial (we'll provide an estimate for a 30-day reserved capacity)?

—
Marissa
Attachments: prompt_set_v1.txt, latency_benchmarks_50k_tokens.csv, mutual_action_plan_Finteq_v1.pdf

Subject: Re: Demo recap: model choices & risk assessment

Marissa — thanks for the detail and the quick turnaround. Olivia and I reviewed the attachments. We're aligned to move forward with the PoC and confirm the following:
- Traffic slice: start with 25% of session-creation traffic (~80 req/s peak)
- SLO: p95 end-to-end <= 450ms for critical flows (we accept higher latency for non-critical summarization)
- Procurement: start with Hosted PoC credits for the 5-day evaluation; we'll revisit Dedicated if the OpenMosaic route is chosen for rollout.

Please send the PoC runbook and the access invite for the evaluation workspace. We'll loop in our infra lead after you share the runbook.

—Daniel
